body: It's [off by default](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/conf/eslint.json). We have [a test](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/5037dd38efe969bdac4e4816b5502340e8f21408/Makefile.js#L290-L293) ensuring this sort of thing doesn't happen.

Hm. I did a search on the project for the string `no-mixed-requires` and after my removal from `.eslintrc` the only occurences are within `./node_modules/grunt-eslint/node_modules/eslint/`. And yet:

```
$ grunt eslint                                                                                                      22.05 16:52:51
Running "eslint:all" (eslint) task

grunt/config/connect.js
  9:0  error  Do not mix 'require' and other declarations  no-mixed-requires

grunt/tasks/css-inline-image-size.js
  9:0  error  Do not mix 'require' and other declarations  no-mixed-requires

grunt/tasks/css-inline-images.js
  9:0  error  Do not mix 'require' and other declarations  no-mixed-requires

✖ 3 problems

Warning: Task "eslint:all" failed. Use --force to continue.

Aborted due to warnings.
```
Do you have any other .eslintrc's in parent directories above the directory you're running from? A recent fix was made to pull those in.
I don't have `.eslintrc` files in any directory up from the project directory to `/`.

Doesn't the `node` environment set this option to `2`?
https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/5037dd38efe969bdac4e4816b5502340e8f21408/conf/environments.json#L372

Which means that this issue applies to every rule changed in that block:

```
        "rules": {
            "no-catch-shadow": 0,
            "no-console": 0,
            "no-global-strict": 0,
            "no-mixed-requires": 2,
            "no-new-require": 2,
            "no-path-concat": 2,
            "handle-callback-err": [2, "err"],
            "no-process-exit": 2
        }
```
True. IMO docs are unclear on what happens here. But it's especially confusing in the `no-mixed-requires` case as `require` happens almost exclusively in the `node` context.

I'm not sure if we have a way to automatically make this clear. To me, "off by default" means that if you don't do anything else, the rule will be off. If you flip the Node.js environment on, you're not really working in the default setting anymore.

If you have suggestions on how to make this clearer, I'm definitely open to them.
We could add ({on, off} by default in 'node' environment), and a check for that in checkRuleFiles.

The problem is it doesn't seem to be currently documented which rules specific environments change & how, one has to look into the `environment.json` file to see that.

IMO it should either go into rules.md in a similar fashion as @jrajav mentioned or there should be a more detailed description of what specific environments change.
If someone wants to take a stab at automating the additional details in the docs, I'm for it.

issue.body:
This change adds info to the docs about rules that have been overridden in [the environments.json config](conf/environments.json):

[Rules README.md](docs/rules/README.md):

> - [handle-callback-err](handle-callback-err.md) - enforces error handling in callbacks (off by default)
> - [handle-callback-err](handle-callback-err.md) - enforces error handling in callbacks (off by default) **(on by default in the node environment)**

It also adds validation to [Makefile.js](Makefile.js) to verify that the environment settings are listed in the docs. If a rule has specifically been set for an environment, its setting must be in the docs, whether it was turned on or off. The idea is that a rule will only be set for an environment if it differs from the default.

This is meant to address #918.
